edges.description: PPP1R21 is the structural backbone of the FERRY complex; a disease-causing truncation removes the binding site for TBCK and FERRY3 and the truncated complex no longer binds Rab5.
Loss of PPP1R21 slows the clearance of endocytosed transferrin from patient fibroblasts without affecting its uptake.
Fibroblasts from a patient homozygous for a PPP1R21 splice variant show activated proteasome function and protein aggregates; the steps between PPP1R21 loss and proteasome activation are not known.

Inferred: the endo-lysosomal defect is documented only in fibroblasts, and no neural model of PPP1R21 deficiency has been studied, so how it produces the white matter, callosal and cerebellar abnormalities is unknown.

nodes.description: Structural brain abnormalities are part of the syndrome: thinning of the corpus callosum, reduced cerebral white matter volume, delayed myelination, ventricular enlargement and cerebellar vermis hypoplasia. Together with the profound developmental impairment, they define an early-onset encephalopathy.

nodes.description: PPP1R21 forms the backbone of the five-subunit endosomal Rab5 and RNA/ribosome intermediary (FERRY) complex (TBCK, PPP1R21, FERRY3/C12orf4, CRYZL1, GATD1), which binds GTP-bound Rab5 on early endosomes and is proposed to carry mRNA for local translation. With TBCK and FERRY3, PPP1R21 also forms a heterotrimer with RAB5 GTPase-activating activity. Whether the endocytic defect in patient cells is mediated through the FERRY complex is not established.
